subject: Field report: unexpected fallback when requests include '##' prefix
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-data.com>, Sofia Patel <sofia.patel@acme-data.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Quick question on prefix behavior — saw fallback in-prod

Hi Liam / Sofia,

Thanks again for the call earlier. A quick heads-up: your team hit a case where requests containing a leading "##" token cause the request to silently route to our lower-tier model variant (fallback) for ~30% of calls, which degraded output. Can you confirm whether you intentionally add that prefix in the generation prompts?

If yes, we want to validate whether it's the prompt normalization or our routing policy treating the prefix as a detection signal. Looping in Dev and Marcus to triage on the platform/runtime side.

Next steps I'd like:
- Acme: paste a sanitized example of the failing prompt (if possible)
- Internal: Dev/Marcus, can you confirm whether a special token triggers model-variant fallback?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick screen share.

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

Attachment: none in this message
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-data.com>

Cc: Sofia Patel <sofia.patel@acme-data.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on prefix behavior — saw fallback in-prod

Hey Stephanie — thanks for flagging. We do include a short metadata marker at times that looks like '##source=ingest' at the top of prompts for downstream processing. We didn't expect that to affect routing.

I've attached a sanitized prompt example and a small batch of logs showing the request ids. Let me know what else you need.

— Liam
Liam O'Connor
Lead ML Engineer, Acme Data Solutions

Attachments: acme_prefix_bug_logs.zip
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-data.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on prefix behavior — saw fallback in-prod

Thanks for the samples, Liam — reproducing locally now. Initial notes:

- The batching/ routing policy has a regex-based signal that looks for certain line-prefix patterns to enable a conservative fallback when a prompt has potentially long-throughput characteristics. It was originally intended for markers like 'SYSTEM:' or '<<DOC>>', but the current implementation erroneously treats a standalone '##' prefix as a signal.
- I've attached a runtime trace that shows the decision point (INF_ROUTER_MATCH) and the matched pattern.

Immediate mitigation options we can take (pros/cons):
1) Adjust the regex to require an explicit keyword after '##' (e.g., '##source=') — low risk, medium rollout time.
2) Add a short whitelist for existing Acme customer markers (fast but brittle).
3) Disable that particular detection entirely for the hosted tier while we ship a deterministic classifier (higher risk to unit economics).

For this week, I propose (1) as the safest path: narrow the regex and push a minor routing-rule config. If Acme is comfortable, we can also add a customer-level override so your traffic won't be affected while the fix rolls out.

I'll open INF-8791 and paste the traces.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime

Appreciate the triage, Dev. Two asks from product/field:

- Can we get a short playbook for SEs outlining a temporary workaround (e.g., Acme remove/escape '##' at the ingestion point or set per-customer override) so they can avoid service disruption today?
- Prioritize the regex narrowing as a patch with a canary rollout and a rollback plan. This is affecting an active expansion deal (DEAL-4218) so we need a tight SLA on mitigation.

Stephanie — can you confirm whether Acme will accept the per-customer override while we push a global fix? If yes, I'll request the override from Ops and coordinate the canary.

— Marissa

1) Acme confirmed they're OK with a temporary per-customer override while Redwood ships the patch. Liam will disable the prefix in their ingestion if needed, but prefers the override for minimal operational churn.
2) Dev is preparing a regex-narrowing patch and will canary it to 10% of traffic tomorrow; INF-8791 is the tracking ticket.
3) Marissa drafted a short SE playbook (attached) with recommended customer messaging, quick detection steps, and the per-customer override request template.

Action items:
